{{Nihongo|'''Akito Arima''', [[Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire|KBE]]|有馬 朗人|Arima Akito|13 September 1930 – 7 December 2020}} was a Japanese [[nuclear physics|nuclear physicist]], politician, and haiku poet, known for the [[interacting boson model]].<ref>Arima, Iachello ''Collective nuclear states as representations of a SU(6) Group'', Physical Review Letters 35, 1069–1072 (1975).</ref><ref>Arima, Iachello ''The interacting boson model'', Cambridge University Press, 1987.</ref><ref>Arima, Iachello ''Interacting boson model of collective states'', Part 1 (the vibrational limit) Annals of Physics 99, 253-317 (1976), Part 2 (the rotational limit) ibid. 111, 201-238 (1978), Part 3 (the transition from SU (5) to SU (3)), ibid. 115, 325-366 (1978), Part 4 (the O(6) limit) ibid. 123, 468-492 (1979).</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1146/annurev.ns.31.120181.000451| doi-access=free| title=The Interacting Boson Model| year=1981| last1=Arima| first1=A.| last2=Iachello| first2=F.| journal=[[Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science]]| volume=31| pages=75–105| bibcode=1981ARNPS..31...75A}}</ref>

==Early life and career==
Arima was born 1930 in [[Osaka]]. He studied at the [[University of Tokyo]], where he received his doctorate in 1958. He became a research associate at the [[Institute for Nuclear Studies (Tokyo)|Institute for Nuclear Studies]] in 1956.

Arima became a lecturer in 1960, and an associate professor at the Department of Physics in 1964 at the University of Tokyo. He was promoted to a full professor in 1975. He was president of the University of Tokyo during 1989–1993. In 1993, he moved to [[Hosei University]]. Since 1993, he has been scientific adviser of the [[Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (Japan)|Ministry of Education]] and from 1993 to 1998 president of [[RIKEN]].<ref>[http://www.jspsusa.org/FORUM1997/bio.arima.html Biography], Japan Society for the Promotion of Science.</ref><ref>[http://www.jst.go.jp/astf/document/13cv.pdf Curriculum Vitae] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171118224451/http://www.jst.go.jp/astf/document/13cv.pdf |date=2017-11-18 }}, Japan Science and Technology Agency.</ref>

He was a visiting professor at [[Rutgers University]], [[New Jersey]] (1967–1968), and a professor at the [[State University of New York]] at [[Stony Brook, New York|Stony Brook]] (1971–1973). In 1974, he founded the [[interacting boson model]] with [[Francesco Iachello]].
[[File:Dr Arima Lecture Okinawa Keieisha Kyoukai (33202998854) (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|Arima in 2011]]
In 1998 he entered the [[Diet of Japan]] as a member of the [[House of Councillors]] for the [[Liberal Democratic Party (Japan)|Liberal Democratic Party]]. He was Minister of Education until 1999 under the government of [[Keizo Obuchi]]. After the cabinet reshuffle in 1999, he served as Director of the Science Museum. From 2000 he was chairman of the [[Japan Science Foundation]].

Arima has served as the Chancellor of Musashi Academy of the Nezu Foundation since 2006.<ref>[[:ja:有馬朗人|有馬朗人]], Akito Arima - Japanese Wikipedia Entry</ref><ref>[http://www.musashi.ac.jp/english/about/president.html], Musashi University Website</ref>

==Death==
Arima died from [[heart failure]] on December 7, 2020, at the age of 90.<ref>[https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXZQODG074HG0X01C20A2000000 有馬朗人氏死去　元東大学長・文相、90歳] {{in lang|ja}}</ref> He was posthumously promoted to the [[List of Japanese court ranks, positions and hereditary titles|court rank]] of Senior Third Rank (''shosanmi'' or ''ōkimi no tsunokurai''), which is usually awarded to high-ranking politicians and prominent scholars in post-war Japan.<ref>『官報』令和3年1月13日 第410号 7頁</ref>

==Awards and honors==
* [[Nishina Memorial Prize]] (1978)
* Honorary Professor, the [[University of Glasgow]] (1984)
* [[Humboldt Award]] (1987)
* [[Haiku Society]] Prize for a book of poetry ([[haiku]] poems) (1988)<ref>Arima '' [http://www.brooksbookshaiku.com/translations/arimahaiku.html Einstein's Century: Akito Arima's Haiku]'', Brooks Books, 2001.</ref>
* [[John Price Wetherill Medal]] of the [[Franklin Institute]] (1990)
* Grand Cross of the [[Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany]] (1990)
* [[Military William Order]] (1991)
* Honorary Doctor, [[Drexel University]] (1992)
* Honorary Professor, the University of Science and Technology, China (1992)
* Honorary Doctor, [[Chung Yuan Christian University]], Taiwan (1992)
* [[Tom W. Bonner Prize in Nuclear Physics|Bonner Prize]] of the [[American Physical Society]] (1993)
* [[Japan Academy Prize (academics)|Japan Academy Prize]] (1993)
* Honorary Doctor, the State University of New York at Stony Brook (1994)
* Honorary Doctor, the [[University of Groningen]] (1994)<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.rug.nl/kvi-cart/organization/history?lang=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170726025140/https://www.rug.nl/kvi-cart/organization/history?lang=en |title=KVI - Center for Advanced Radiation Technology - History |publisher=University of Groningen |date=29 March 2019 |archive-date=26 July 2017}}</ref>
* Honorary Doctor, the [[University of Birmingham]] (1996)
* Grand Officier of the [[Legion of Honour]] (1998)
* Foreign Honorary Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (1999)<ref name=AAAS>{{cite web|title=Book of Members, 1780-2010: Chapter A|url=http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterA.pdf|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|access-date=22 April 2011| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110510021801/http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterA.pdf| archive-date= 10 May 2011 | url-status= live}}</ref>
*Honorary Knight Commander of the [[Order of the British Empire]] (KBE) (2002)
*[[Person of Cultural Merit]] (2004)
*Grand Cordon of the [[Order of the Rising Sun]] (2004)
*[[Order of Culture]] (2010)
* [[Dakotsu Prize]] (2018)
